text:
Dear Dr. Mercer,

Thank you for agreeing to see this 32-year-old female patient who initially developed progressive breathlessness on exertion alongside a persistent, dry, non-phlegm-producing cough around two years ago. She works in office administration, does not smoke, and takes only a daily multivitamin. Her family medical history is non-contributory.

Her recent pulmonary function testing showed a clear restrictive impairment with reduced total capacity. A high-resolution chest CT revealed extensive subpleural cluster cysts, widespread fibrosing interstitial changes, and marked traction dilatation of the bronchial tree. Thoracoabdominal imaging excluded any occult neoplastic process or solid tumor.

In parallel with her respiratory decline, she has manifested distinctive cutaneous and mucosal alterations. On examination, there is a fine, net-like cutaneous hyperpigmentation across her neck, as well as splitting, thinning, and severe structural degradation of all fingernails. Oral inspection reveals adherent white keratotic plaques coating the bilateral buccal mucosa. A punch biopsy documented pronounced stratum corneum thickening accompanied by loss of epidermal cell cohesion.

Laboratory evaluations show normal quantitative immunoglobulins and intact lymphocyte subsets, ruling out impaired immunity. Her dilated ophthalmologic examination was unremarkable, demonstrating a completely flat macula without neurosensory elevation or subretinal fluid. Furthermore, she experienced no childhood developmental lag and achieved normal expected adult stature.

Given the multisystem involvement, I would appreciate your comprehensive assessment and advice on appropriate diagnostic avenues and subsequent management.

Sincerely,
Dr. Julian Vance
